## About

I am a researcher (*chargé de recherches*) at the [Institut national d'études démographiques (Ined)](https://www.ined.fr), based in Aubervilliers, France.

As an economist and demographer, my research focuses mainly on **the long-run dynamics of spatial demographic and economic divergence in France and Europe**.

I am co-director of the [French Regional Database](https://frdata.org/en/) and currently an elected member of INED's board of directors.

**Adress**: 9 cours des Humanités, 93322 Aubervilliers Cedex, France\
**E-mail**: florian.bonnet#ined.fr

## Current research projects

-   **Deaths of despair in Europe**: Is the increase in deaths of despair seen in the United States in recent decades also evident in specific geographical areas of Europe?

-   **Extreme longevity in France**: Did the probability of reaching the age of 100 differ significantly depending on place of birth for cohorts born in the early 20th century who have since passed away?

-   **Epidemiological transition in Paris**: How have differences in life expectancy and cause-specific mortality between Parisian neighbourhoods and districts evolved from the late 19th century to the present day?

-   **Regional income distributions in Europe**: Using tax statistics, is it possible to locate individuals with the highest incomes in Western Europe at a granular level and see how this distribution has changed since 1990?
